title: Ciscomani Wraps Up Successful August District Work Period Across Arizona’s 6th District
text:
Tucson, AZ - Representative Juan Ciscomani concluded a productive August District Work Period, traveling nearly 2,500 miles across Arizona’s 6th Congressional District for 50 in-person events to meet with constituents, visit local businesses and community organizations, hear directly from local leaders, and highlight millions of dollars in federal investments he has helped secure for the district.

Throughout the district work period, Representative Ciscomani emphasized his commitment to amplifying Southern Arizonans' Arizona 6th Congressional District voices in Washington and transforming local priorities into meaningful legislative action.

"Getting out into the district and hearing directly from the people I represent is one of the most important parts of my job," said Representative Ciscomani. "From healthcare providers and veterans to educators, small business owners, law enforcement, and families, these conversations give me a firsthand understanding of what our communities need. I am taking these perspectives back to Washington to continue fighting for real solutions that make a difference right here in Southern Arizona."

Ciscomani’s outreach included a robust schedule of meetings, roundtables, and site visits, ensuring constituent voices shape his policy priorities.

A major focus of the August District Work Period was highlighting the impact of $42.7 million in preliminary federal funding Representative Ciscomani has advocated for across 20 Community Project Funding (CPF) requests in the Fiscal Year 2027 appropriations bills.

Ciscomani visited communities across the district to see firsthand how these investments will address local priorities, including public safety, transportation, healthcare, workforce development, and infrastructure.

Among the projects highlighted were:

$6.76 million for Eloy for the Frontier Street Mill & Overlay Project.

$4.2 million for the Oro Valley Police Department to equip its new headquarters with critical technology and equipment.

$3 million for Marana to improve the Interstate 10 interchange at Exit 236 and address growing transportation needs.

$2 million for Benson Hospital to expand critical healthcare services in rural Cochise County.

$2.7 million for Pima JTED to expand career and technical education programs preparing students for high-demand careers.

$1.7 million for the Town of Duncan for flood mitigation and pedestrian safety improvements.

$1.6 million for Pinal Airpark to advance development of a new air traffic control tower.

$1.3 million for Huachuca City’s Fire Department for a new quint ladder truck.

$1 million for the Cochise County Sheriff’s Office to strengthen emergency communications capabilities across the county.

"These investments are about more than a line item on a spreadsheet; they are about turning Arizona priorities into a reality. Each project was selected to ensure these federal dollars have the greatest possible impact on our local communities," Ciscomani said.

Read news coverage of Ciscomani’s Community Project Funding visits HERE, HERE, and HERE.

The congressman spent time with local healthcare leaders throughout the district, hearing directly about the challenges facing patients and providers. In Pima County, he met with leadership at Pima Heart & Vascular. In Cochise County, Ciscomani visited Benson Hospital to see firsthand how the $2 million in preliminary federal funding he secured will help expand critical healthcare access in rural Southern Arizona. He also visitedChiricahua Community Health Center to discuss broader efforts to expand quality care in underserved communities.

Read news coverage of the congressman’s healthcare visits and roundtables HERE and HERE.

Ciscomani also continued his work supporting Southern Arizona’s veterans, meeting with members of his Veterans Advisory Council to provide an update on the 19 veterans bills he has introduced this Congress, many of which were shaped by conversations with veterans across the district. To honor the invaluable contributions of local veterans, Ciscomani hosted his fifth Veteran Servant Leader Award Ceremony, the first of which to be held in Sierra Vista. This event honored 19 local veterans for their continued service and leadership, as well as one civilian for his lasting support of the local veteran community.

For more information on the Veteran Servant Leader Awards and Veterans Advisory Council meeting, click HERE.

Education and workforce development remained another key focus of the August District Work Period. Ciscomani visited Pima JTED alongside SBA Deputy Administrator Bill Briggs to highlight the $2.7 million in preliminary federal funding secured for the expansion of Innovation Tech High School. The investment will expand programs in heavy equipment operation, construction technology, engineering, bioscience, sustainability, and other high-demand fields.

He also recognized outstanding educators at the American Dream Inspirational Educator Awards and met with students from underserved communities who received scholarships from the Lapan Sunshine Foundation. Ciscomani emphasized that career and technical education provides students with a direct pathway toward good-paying careers while helping Arizona employers meet the demand for a skilled workforce. At Buena High School, he visited 13 different career and technical education classes offered to local students.

Ciscomani met with entrepreneurs, business owners, and local job creators throughout the district, including at the 2026 SPARK Business Summit hosted by the Marana Chamber of Commerce and Better Business Bureau of Southern Arizona. He also joined the Marana Chamber of Commerce for its Member Appreciation Luncheon and recognized local business leaders and employers who continue to strengthen the community. He also welcomed a new favorite to the Marana community for the grand opening of Dickey’s Barbecue Pit, celebrating local entrepreneurship and Arizona’s small-business community.

Ciscomani also hosted Speaker Mike Johnson and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent at the PepsiCo manufacturing facility in Casa Grande for a roundtable with local manufacturers followed by a press conference.

The discussion focused on how the Working Families Tax Cuts Act is supporting Arizona manufacturing, encouraging investment, creating jobs, and delivering tax relief to hardworking families. The roundtable brought together PepsiCo leadership and other local manufacturers to discuss the impact of policies including No Tax on Overtime, incentives for new factories and facility expansions, and 100% expensing for capital investments.

Read news coverage of the manufacturing press conference HERE.

Additionally, Ciscomani met with pastors and faith leaders from across Arizona’s 6th Congressional District to discuss challenges facing congregations and ways Congress can better support faith-based organizations serving Arizona families. Conversations centered on strengthening communities, expanding affordable housing, strengthening public safety, and ensuring families feel secure in their places of worship.

He also attended a naturalization ceremony in Tucson, where he shared his own story of becoming a United States citizen 20 years ago and experiencing the American Dream firsthand.

The congressman closed out the productive district work period by joining the Marana High School Tigers and Salpointe Catholic Lancers for their season-opening football game, where he participated in the ceremonial coin toss. Ciscomani’s efforts during the August District Work Period come as he continues to be recognized for his bipartisan approach to governing.

BridgeGrades recently ranked Representative Ciscomani as the most bipartisan member of Arizona’s congressional delegation in either the House or Senate, and among the top 20 most bipartisan members of Congress overall, Republican or Democrat. The recognition highlights Ciscomani’s commitment to working across the aisle and delivering results for Arizona’s 6th Congressional District.

As the congressman is now back in Washington, he is encouraged by this productive August District Work period and looks forward to continuing to fight for Southern Arizona’s needs and priorities at the federal level.

title: Rep. Clyde Leads GA GOP Delegation in Urging Attorney General Carr to Clarify Georgia Law Following Historic NFA Court Ruling
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congressman Andrew Clyde (GA-09) led seven of his Georgia Republican colleagues in sending a letter to Georgia Attorney General Chris Carr urging him to issue a legal opinion clarifying a discrepancy in Georgia law that could prevent law-abiding Georgians from fully exercising their recently restored Second Amendment rights following the landmark ruling in Silencer Shop Foundation v. ATF (consolidated with Jensen v. ATF).

The lawmakers open by highlighting Attorney General Carr’s decision to have the State of Georgia join as a plaintiff in the case that helped deliver the most significant Second Amendment restoration in more than a century.

“We congratulate you on your win in having the State of Georgia join as a plaintiff in the Silencer Shop Foundation v. ATF case, in which the United States District Court for the Northern District of Texas ruled on August 5th, 2026 that the National Firearms Act (NFA) registration and transfer requirements are unconstitutional because it cannot survive the elimination of the underlying taxes. Congressional efforts to eliminate those taxes, combined with this court ruling, reflect the greatest restoration of Georgians’ Second Amendment rights in over 100 years.”

However, Rep. Clyde and his colleagues explain that Georgia’s current criminal code prevents Georgians from freely and fully exercising their recently restored Second Amendment liberties.

“Georgia’s criminal code generally prohibits possession of short-barreled shotguns, short-barreled rifles, machine guns, and silencers. That prohibition does not apply, however, to a person ‘who is authorized to possess the same because he has registered the sawed-off shotgun, sawed-off rifle, machine gun, dangerous weapon, or silencer in accordance with the dictates of the National Firearms Act.’ Now that NFA registration is no longer required and, under the court’s ruling, may no longer lawfully be demanded of Georgians covered by the injunction, this provision no longer maps cleanly onto federal law. Read literally, it could be misunderstood to condition Georgia’s exemption on an act of federal registration that a covered person is no longer required, or even permitted, to complete. This ambiguity has deterred Georgians, who are in full compliance with all applicable federal law, from fully exercising their Second Amendment rights, out of a well-founded fear that doing so could place them in violation of Georgia’s criminal code.”

Therefore, Rep. Clyde and his colleagues urge Attorney General Carr to issue clear guidance on the matter to ensure Georgians can fully enjoy their Second Amendment freedoms as the Founders intended.

“Georgia gun owners and purchasers need guidance and clarity from your office to be able to fully celebrate this tremendous Second Amendment victory. We thank you again for your leadership in securing this outcome for the Peach State, and we look forward to working with you to ensure this historic restoration of Americans’ Second Amendment freedoms is properly applied to our fellow Georgians.”

Read the full letter HERE.

Cosigners include Representatives Rick Allen (GA-12), Buddy Carter (GA-01), Mike Collins (GA-10), Clay Fuller (GA-14), Brian Jack (GA-03), Barry Loudermilk (GA-11), and Rich McCormick (GA-07).

Background

Due to Rep. Clyde’s hard-fought efforts, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act includes a provision to zero out the $200 tax on suppressors and short-barreled firearms under the draconian NFA, mirroring parts of Clyde’s Stop Harassing Owners of Rifles Today (SHORT) Act and Constitutional Hearing Protection Act.

However, the burdensome transfer and registration requirements linked to the $0 tax remained — despite the fact that it was Congress’s clear intent to repeal NFA registration by eliminating NFA taxation.

Therefore, Rep. Clyde led Republican lawmakers in urging the DOJ to adopt this congressional intent in all litigation (letters to the-Attorney General Bondi available HERE and HERE). As a member of the House Appropriations Committee, the Congressman has also fought to eliminate NFA registration for suppressors and short-barreled firearms through the annual appropriations process.

On August 5th, the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas delivered a monumental win to plaintiffs in Silencer Shop Foundation v. ATF. The landmark ruling struck down NFA registration requirements for suppressors, short-barreled rifles (SBRs), short-barreled shotguns (SBSs), and any other weapons (AOWs), rightly ruling that these requirements exceed Congress’s constitutional authority after Congress eliminated the NFA’s transfer and making taxes on those arms.

title: BREAKING: DOJ RULING OUTLINES NEW PATH TO STRIP FEDERAL FUNDING FROM STATES THAT DON’T AID TRUMP’S MASS DEPORTATION PUSH
text:
Washington, DC – U.S. Representative Lou Correa (CA-46) condemned a new Department of Justice (DOJ) legal opinion issued today that outlines a path for the federal government to strip funding from states that don’t help carry out the Trump administration’s mass deportation agenda.

“This is a blatant attempt to turn every state government in the country into an arm of ICE,” Correa said. “Families apply for food assistance and disability benefits because they need help feeding their kids and caring for their parents. Now this administration wants to hold those programs hostage to advance its violent and inhumane deportation agenda that tears communities apart.”

“My team and I are looking into the legality of this interpretation. This administration has its own unique way of interpreting the law. California already sends the federal government more than $80 billion a year in federal taxes than we get back. Clearly, this administration wants more from us,” Correa concluded.

The DOJ’s Office of Legal Counsel adopted a new interpretation that says when states accept federal funding to help assist low-income families, seniors, and people with disabilities, all state agencies have to report people’s immigration status to the U.S. Department of Homeland Security. This includes widely used programs like Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) and Supplemental Security Income (SSI). The opinion significantly broadens who must comply. Previously, only the specific state agencies administering the federal funding programs were required to report.

title: CORREA DEMANDS ANSWERS ON TRUMP ADMINISTRATION’S PLAN TO HAND OVER YOSEMITE LAND TO PRIVATE DEVELOPERS
text:
Washington, DC – U.S. Representative Lou Correa (CA-46) today sent a letter to Interior Secretary Doug Burgum and National Park Service Comptroller Jessica Bowron demanding transparency and answers over the Trump Administration’s alleged proposal to parcel off part of Yosemite National Park to a private real estate developer.

“I write in strong opposition to recent reports that the National Park Service (NPS) is working to parcel off part of Yosemite National Park in California to give to a private real-estate developer. Under the alleged proposal, land within Yosemite National Park would be ceded to the developer to construct a road that connects private property to the park,” Correa said.

“I am outraged by this alleged action that threatens Yosemite’s natural resources at the expense of private real-estate developers. Yosemite National Park was created in 1890 and since then our nation has worked together to protect its precious ecosystem and natural wonders, including Half Dome and the giant sequoia trees,” Correa continued. “This agency proposal runs counter to over 135 years of protecting this land in California for both wildlife and the public.”

“The NPS was created in 1916 to protect our precious natural resources and to promote and regulate national parks, monuments, and reservations to “conserve the scenery and the natural and historic objects and the wildlife therein and to provide for the enjoyment of the same in such manner and by such means as will leave them unimpaired for the enjoyment of future generations,” Correa concluded. “This proposed land exchange is contrary to the NPS’s 150 years of work to protect our national parks and Congress’s intent when it created the agency.”

title: CORREA VOTES NO ON GOP EFFORT TO LOCK IN CONSERVATIVE SUPREME COURT
text:
Washington, DC – U.S. Representative Lou Correa (CA-46), member of the House Judiciary Committee, released the following statement following his ‘no’ vote on the GOP constitutional amendment to permanently keep the Supreme Court at nine members, solidifying the bench’s conservative majority.

“The Constitution gives Congress the power of impeachment, oversight, and the purse. Under Trump, Congressional Republicans have surrendered that power again and again to serve the president instead of the people. This amendment is just the latest example of that.

“Congress has repeatedly expanded and shrunk the size of the Supreme Court. There’s no reason to lock in nine justices now except that it works in Republicans’ favor. I’ve never supported packing the Court for political advantage, and I don’t support this further surrender of congressional power.”

title: Rep. Crockett Demands DOJ Investigate Alarming Pattern of Possible Modern-Day Lynchings
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congresswoman Jasmine Crockett (TX-30), Ranking Member of the House Judiciary Subcommittee on Oversight, demanded that the Department of Justice (DOJ) investigate an alarming pattern of Black Americans found hanging from trees across the country.

In a letter to Attorney General Todd Blanche and Assistant Attorney General for Civil Rights Harmeet Dhillon, Crockett called on DOJ to use its nationwide law enforcement capabilities to examine whether deaths that have been treated as isolated incidents and ruled deaths by suicide by state and local authorities, may instead reveal broader patterns of racial animus or systemic investigative failures.

“The images we are seeing of Black bodies hanging from trees and other structures across this country should shock the conscience of every American,” said Congresswoman Crockett. “Given our nation’s horrific history of racial terror and lynching, we cannot simply look the other way when Black Americans are found dead under circumstances that demand answers. Every one of these cases deserves to be taken seriously, investigated thoroughly, and examined in the context of what is happening across the country.”

Crockett also highlighted concerns that law enforcement personnel themselves may be implicated in some cases. The letter cites a report finding 23 possible modern-day lynching cases involving police or correctional officers and highlights recent revelations concerning racist conduct within the Senatobia Police Department in Mississippi.

“America spent generations allowing Black people to be lynched while institutions with the power to intervene stood by and did nothing,” Crockett said. “We cannot repeat that history. DOJ has the authority, the resources, and the responsibility to determine whether these deaths are isolated tragedies or evidence of something far more sinister. I am demanding that they use them.”

The full letter can be found here.

title: House Veterans’ Affairs Committee Unanimously Passes Rep. Maxine Dexter’s Motion to Subpoena Oracle Leaders Over $27 Billion VA Contract
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, the House Committee on Veterans’ Affairs unanimously passed Congresswoman Maxine Dexter, M.D.’s (OR-03) motion to subpoena Oracle Executive Chairman Larry Ellison and Oracle CEO Mike Sicillia to testify before the House Committee on Veterans’ Affairs about the Department of Veterans Affairs’ (VA) electronic health record modernization contract. The committee Chairman, Mike Bost, had previously invited Oracle to appear in today’s hearing and after initially accepting the invitation, Oracle then declined to participate.

Last month, the VA raised the ceiling on Oracle’s electronic health record modernization contract from $10 billion to over $27 billion through a no-bid extension. Congresswoman Dexter called on Oracle executives to testify under oath about the $17 billion increase, the company’s performance, and whether veterans and taxpayers are getting what they were promised.

“When the company responsible for a taxpayer-funded contract that could grow from $10 billion to roughly $27 billion refuses to sit before Congress and answer questions, this committee cannot fully do its job,” Rep. Dexter said. “Veterans deserve a health records system that works, and taxpayers deserve to know their money is being spent responsibly. A private, closed-door roundtable cannot replace public congressional oversight. Oracle’s leaders must appear before this committee and answer for this contract.”

“As the Ranking Member of the Veterans’ Affairs Committee, I demand accountability from Big Tech profiting off of VA contracts,” said House Committee on Veterans’ Affairs Ranking Member Mark Takano. “Our veterans deserve nothing less than full transparency and responsible stewardship of taxpayer dollars. I commend Dr. Dexter for fighting for this subpoena—an essential step to ensure Congress is holding accountable those responsible for the ballooning Electronic Health Record Modernization budget. I am pleased our Republican colleagues joined us in voting to issue subpoenas. I look forward to hearing from Mr. Ellison and Mr. Sicilia to understand where this money will go and whether veterans are actually getting a good deal.”

The Congresswoman also raised questions about potential conflicts of interest. President Trump’s 2026 financial disclosures included transactions involving Oracle securities, and The Wall Street Journal reported that Ellison gave roughly $45 million to a political nonprofit supporting Trump’s 2024 election effort.

“I am not saying this is a corrupt contract, but the red flags demand serious scrutiny,” Rep. Dexter said. “This is a $17 billion no-bid increase for a company with a troubled performance record, whose founder spent heavily to support the president and whose stock appears in the president’s financial disclosures. Congress has a responsibility to investigate.”

Background:

Congresswoman Dexter, a former VA doctor, has heard concerns from VA doctors about Oracles’ system. She also cited Oregon’s troubled experience with Oracle’s work on the state’s health insurance marketplace. Oregon sued Oracle in 2014, and the dispute was resolved through a 2016 settlement of over $100 million.

The Government Accountability Office (GAO) has repeatedly raised concerns about the VA’s electronic health record modernization effort. As of August 2026, VA had not fully implemented 14 of GAO’s 18 recommendations related to cost estimates, scheduling, program management, user adoption, satisfaction and operational testing.

The committee’s unanimous passage of Congresswoman Dexter’s motion advances subpoenas calling for Ellison and Sicilia to testify at a public hearing. Their testimony would allow committee members to question Oracle’s leaders directly about the company’s work and demand answers for veterans and taxpayers.

title: DOWNING INTRODUCES NO HUD FUNDING FOR SANCTUARY CITIES ACT
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congressman Troy Downing (MT-02) introduced HR 10222, the No HUD Funding for Sanctuary Cities Act, legislation that would make sanctuary jurisdictions ineligible for grant funding administered by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD).

Under current law, jurisdictions that refuse to cooperate with federal immigration enforcement can still receive HUD grant funding. The No HUD Funding for Sanctuary Cities Act would end that practice and ensure federal housing dollars are not directed to sanctuary jurisdictions.

“If a sanctuary city is not complying with federal law, we should not allocate American taxpayers’ hard-earned money to those areas,” said Congressman Downing. “The American taxpayer should not be responsible for funding cities that choose to disregard federal immigration policy while law-abiding citizens are left to bear the cost.”

Read the full bill text HERE.

Statements of Support:

“Sanctuary jurisdictions should not be rewarded with federal housing dollars while refusing to cooperate with federal immigration law. Rep. Downing’s No HUD Funding for Sanctuary Cities Act puts American taxpayers first and ensures federal resources are directed to communities that uphold the law rather than undermine it.”

Michael Hough, Co-President, NumbersUSA

“The number of sanctuary cities in the U.S. has surged in recent years, offering taxpayer-funded public services and housing assistance to millions of illegal aliens while blocking immigration enforcement. At the same time, mass illegal immigration has driven up housing demand, worsened affordability, and burdened public benefits programs. The No HUD Funding for Sanctuary Cities Act takes commonsense steps to put an end to sanctuary cities and illegal immigration rather than rewarding those who break our laws. FAIR applauds Congressman Downing for putting Americans first and urges Congress to swiftly pass this bill."

Joe Chatam, Director of Government Relations, Federation for American Immigration Reform

"Sanctuary jurisdictions that obstruct immigration enforcement are the weak links driving illegal immigration across the country. It is fundamentally unfair to hardworking Americans that these cities and States can harbor illegal aliens while simultaneously taking federal housing funds. We thank Rep. Downing for introducing the No HUD Funding for Sanctuary Cities Act, which finally cuts off taxpayer dollars to jurisdictions that think they are above the law."

Grant Newman, Director of Government Relations, Immigration Accountability Project

The No HUD Funding for Sanctuary Cities Act is cosponsored by:

Rep. Warren Davidson (OH-08), Rep. Pete Sessions (TX-17), Rep. Barry Loudermilk (GA-11), Rep. Scott Fitzgerald (WI-05), Rep. Rich McCormick (GA-07), Rep. Scott Perry (PA-10), Rep. Michael Cloud (TX-27), Rep. Barry Moore (AL-01), Rep. Harriet Hageman (WY-At Large), Rep. Buddy Carter (GA-01), Rep. Ben Cline (VA-06), Rep. Randy Weber (TX-14), Rep. Josh Brecheen (OK-02), Rep. Sheri Biggs (SC-03), Rep. Andy Harris (MD-01), Rep. Brian Babin (TX-36), and Rep. Michael Rulli (OH-06).

Background:

According to research from the Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, immigration from 2021 to 2024 accounted for approximately 30 percent of the increase in U.S. home prices during that period.

The No HUD Funding for Sanctuary Cities Act would establish that sanctuary jurisdictions are not eligible to receive HUD grant funding for use in those jurisdictions.

title: Rep. Foster Introduces Bill to Improve Financial Sector Security Amid Rising AI Risks
text:
Washington, DC — Today, Congressman Bill Foster (D-IL) introduced legislation to strengthen oversight of technology service providers that support the financial services industry as advances in artificial intelligence (AI) create new risks for financial institutions and their customers.

The Strengthening Oversight for the Financial Sector Act would give the National Credit Union Administration (NCUA) and the Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA) the authority to oversee third-party vendors used by the entities they regulate. This authority, which is available to other federal financial regulators, had been temporarily granted to the NCUA, but has since expired, leaving a dangerous gap in oversight.

As AI makes it easier to identify and exploit vulnerabilities, reliance on third-party technology vendors could provide an attractive opening for attacks on financial institutions. This bill would close that gap and help protect consumers, financial institutions, and the broader financial system from outside threats.

“As AI makes cyberattacks more sophisticated, it is even more important to ensure that third-party vendors don’t become a weak link in our financial system,” said Rep. Foster. “We have learned the hard way how much damage supply chain vulnerabilities can cause, and third-party vendors are attractive targets. This bill will give regulators the tools they need to better protect Americans’ money and sensitive data as AI-assisted cyber threats grow.”

The authority to oversee third-party vendors has been requested by NCUA and FHFA directors from both political parties. The Government Accountability Office and the Financial Stability Oversight Council have made similar recommendations regarding the need for oversight of third-party vendors' vulnerabilities to AI risk.

A version of this legislation passed the House Financial Services Committee in the 117th Congress, but did not receive a floor vote.

A copy of the bill is available here.

title: Franklin Secures $2.9 Million For Public Safety Innovation Lab At Florida Poly
text:
Congressman Scott Franklin (FL-18) today announced he secured $2.9 million for Florida Polytechnic University to establish a new Public Service Applied Innovation Laboratory (PSAIL).

“Florida Poly is doing important work to prepare the next generation of American innovators and tackle real-world challenges in cybersecurity, artificial intelligence and public safety,” said Congressman Scott Franklin. “As a member of the House Appropriations Committee, I’m pleased we were able to secure $2.9 million to help build on that work. This investment will give students valuable hands-on experience, strengthen our public safety capabilities and help develop the skilled workforce America needs to remain competitive and secure.”

“Congressman Franklin’s leadership and support are helping Florida Poly take a major step forward in developing technologies increasingly critical to our state and nation,” said Dr. Devin Stephenson, president of Florida Polytechnic University. “This $2.9 million investment will give our faculty and students extraordinary opportunities to work at the forefront of cybersecurity and artificial intelligence. It will help build a workforce ready to meet our evolving technology needs and expand Florida Poly’s capacity to address real-world challenges that impact our economy and national security. We are tremendously grateful to Congressman Franklin for his confidence in Florida Poly and his commitment to championing this important work.”

The Public Service Applied Innovation Laboratory will:

Establish an Artificial Intelligence Solutions Lab for applied AI research and partnerships;

Create a Network Operations and Security Center focused on protecting network and information technology systems;

Build secure laboratory and data spaces, including an AI prototype room and cyber range;

Provide equipment and hands-on opportunities for student interns working in each lab; and

Support collaboration with public service and public safety organizations on challenges including emergency management.

The funding, secured by Franklin through the annual appropriations process, will equip existing space on the second floor of Florida Poly’s Gary C. Wendt Engineering Building for applied research, hands-on learning and collaboration. The investment will support equipment for student interns in each lab, two secure and dedicated data spaces, an Artificial Intelligence Solutions Prototype Room and Cyber Range, an AIS Management Cockpit and a Network Operations and Security Operations Center Command Center. Together, these capabilities will give students and faculty the tools to test emerging technologies and work alongside public safety partners to develop solutions to real-world challenges.

The $2.9 million award will be administered through the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) and advances NIST’s federal mission under Section 272 of Title 15 of the U.S. Code to support research, education and partnerships that strengthen American innovation and workforce readiness. The project will help develop skilled talent in cybersecurity, artificial intelligence and other technologies increasingly important to America’s economic and national security.

title: Congressman Gonzalez Advocates for Hands Off Our Boca Chica Beach Act in Congressional Hearing
text:
Additionally, the Hands Off Our Boca Chica Act enjoys strong local support. During today’s hearing, the Congressman submitted written statements of support from Texas State Representative Erin Gamez, Cameron County Judge Eddie Treviño, and SpaceX. All three letters can be viewed here.

Geographic names established by an act of Congress, or those introduced as proposed legislation, are not bound by the BGN. Therefore, Congressman Gonzalez’s bill takes precedence over BGN’s principles, policies, and procedures, preventing future proposals to rename Boca Chica Beach during this Congress from being considered.

The proposal was driven by an individual from Mississippi with no ties to our community and has since faced unanimous opposition from local officials and even SpaceX itself.

People who may disagree about many other issues agreed on this one thing: Boca Chica Beach should remain Boca Chica Beach – a name that dates back to at least 1936.

Although we stopped this particular proposal, the process exposed a much larger problem: A federal committee was preparing to vote on the name change of a historic place in South Texas, they didn’t inform the community and the Representative of the provided notice of the scheduled vote.

But no community should have to depend on a last-minute scramble to make sure its voice is heard in a federal decision affecting its own backyard.

It would also require the Domestic Names Committee to notify the appropriate Member of Congress of a proposed name change that affects their district. It does not, however, prevent future policy updates from the Committee.

We must provide Members of Congress with the tools to do the job our constituents sent us here to do: represent their interests when federal decisions affect their communities.

title: Goodlander Joins House Veterans’ Affairs Subcommittees on Health and Technology Modernization
text:
Washington, D.C. — The House Committee on Veterans Affairs formally welcomed Congresswoman Maggie Goodlander (NH-02) to two subcommittees today, unanimously adopting a resolution to appoint Goodlander to the Subcommittee on Health and Subcommittee on Technology Modernization. Goodlander served as an intelligence officer in the United States Navy Reserve for more than a decade and also serves on the House Armed Services Committee and the House Small Business Committee.

“We make a sacred promise to every American who serves: when they come home, the care and benefits they earned will be there for them. That promise has to work in practice — in every clinic, every claim, and every VA system,” said Congresswoman Maggie Goodlander. “On the Health and Technology Modernization Subcommittees, I will fight to expand veterans’ care in New Hampshire, improve our VA medical center, and make sure the technology veterans and VA workers rely on delivers. I am honored to take on this responsibility, and I won’t quit until every Granite State veteran can get the care they need, when and where they need it.”

Goodlander received a bipartisan welcome from committee leadership and colleagues on the committee during today’s hearing.

“Rep. Maggie Goodlander of New Hampshire will be an outstanding addition to our committee. As a former intelligence officer who served 11 years in the Navy Reserve, Rep. Goodlander brings firsthand experience and a deep understanding of the challenges servicemembers and veterans face,” said Ranking Member Rep. Mark Takano (D-CA-41).

“I’ve enjoyed working with you these past few years, and you’ve done a great job on the House Armed Services Committee. And I tell you, these two committees partner very well with themselves, and being a veteran, you completely understand that. I look forward to working with you on Tech Mod and on main committee. Congratulations,” said Rep. Morgan Luttrell (R-TX-08).

The Health Subcommittee oversees the Veterans Health Administration, including veterans’ medical services, facilities, research, and construction. The Technology Modernization Subcommittee oversees the Department of Veterans Affairs’ technology programs, cybersecurity, data management, and electronic health record system.

BACKGROUND ON GOODLANDER’S ADVOCACY FOR VETERANS, SERVICEMEMBERS, AND MILITARY FAMILIES

Expanding veterans’ health care in New Hampshire: Goodlander helped introduce the Veterans Full-Service Care and Access Act to bring a full-service VA medical center to New Hampshire. She also successfully fought for House passage of a bipartisan amendment advancing that mission and helped pass an amendment supporting robust funding for upgrades at the Manchester VA Medical Center.

Bringing care closer to veterans: Following sustained advocacy by New Hampshire’s congressional delegation, Goodlander welcomed the VA’s new community-based outpatient clinic in West Chesterfield that will expand veterans’ access to primary care, mental health care, specialty care, and other services in the Monadnock Region.

Improving veterans’ health and independence: Goodlander helped usher the Aviator Cancers Examination Study (ACES) Act into law to improve understanding of cancer risks among military aviators and aircrew. She also helps lead the bipartisan Automotive Support Services to Improve Safe Transportation (ASSIST) Act of 2025, which would help disabled veterans obtain medically necessary vehicle adaptations.

Demanding accountability from the VA: Goodlander has demanded answers about VA workforce losses and their effect on care at the Manchester VA Medical Center and other facilities serving New Hampshire veterans.

Standing up for servicemembers, military families, and the Portsmouth Naval Shipyard: Goodlander has led bipartisan legislation to strengthen military readiness and protect America’s public shipyard workforce, including protections against hiring freezes and unjustified workforce reductions. She has also opposed efforts to weaken civil-service protections at Portsmouth Naval Shipyard and helped introduce bipartisan legislation to improve health coverage for military families.

title: PHOTO RELEASE: Gottheimer Attends Wreath-Laying Ceremony at the Pentagon 9/11 Memorial Ahead of 25th Anniversary of September 11th
text:

ARLINGTON, VA — Yesterday, Tuesday, September 1, 2026, U.S. Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) attended a wreath-laying ceremony at the Pentagon Memorial to honor the victims of the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks, in advance of the 25th anniversary. Gottheimer serves as the Co-Chair of the bipartisan House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence review of the 9/11 Commission Report. The review evaluates the progress made on the intelligence-related recommendations produced by the 9/11 Commission Report, released in July 2004, and identifies areas of improvement to protect against the next generation of threats.

Gottheimer has helped lead and pass legislation like the bipartisan Never Forget the Heroes Act, to fully fund the 9/11 Victims Compensation Fund to provide long-overdue support to cover 9/11 survivors, first responders, and their families for injuries, medical expenses, and other benefits.

Gottheimer is continuing to fight to pass the bipartisan FIRE Cancer Act to provide federal investments so that all firefighters can get access to preventative tests, including multi-cancer early detection tests.

title: Congressman Rogers Votes to Protect Mining in America
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – U.S. Rep. Harold “Hal” Rogers (KY-05) voted for the Protecting Domestic Mining Act (H.R. 1501) on Wednesday to expedite permitting for American mining and mineral processing.

“We need to strengthen mining in America, not only to create jobs in the coal industry and lower energy rates, but to empower the U.S. supply chain from mining to manufacturing. Products that are Made in America, ultimately start with Mining in America,” said Congressman Rogers, Dean of the House. “This bill streamlines the permitting process and clears roadblocks for American production, so we don’t have to rely on foreign countries for raw materials.”

Last year, the United States depended on imports for more than half of its supply of 54 non-fuel mineral commodities, giving other countries leverage over American workers, manufacturers and national security.

title: Ranking Member Johnson’s Opening Statement At Hearing On Protecting America’s Patent System And Innovation Economy
text:
Washington, D.C. (September 2, 2026)—Today, Rep. Hank Johnson, Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on Courts, Intellectual Property, Artificial Intelligence, and the Internet, delivered opening remarks at a subcommittee hearing on renewing the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office’s (USPTO) fee-setting authority and protecting a fair, accessible patent system that rewards American innovation and ingenuity.

Thank you, Chairman Issa.

The USPTO’s fee-setting authority has given it the flexibility to move its workers remote, plan its budgets ahead, and tailor fees for small and micro entities. Originally, it was set to expire in just a few days on September the 16th. Yesterday, however, House and Senate Republicans were generous enough to kick the can down the road until after they are reelected. The authority is now set to expire on December 12th, 2026. Failing to reauthorize the USPTO’s fee setting authority risks transforming a traditionally nonpartisan agency into one that serves political ideology over merit.

Ensuring that USPTO remains a beacon of American innovation means not just reauthorizing the fee setting authority but ensuring USPTO advisory committees can continue to advise the USPTO without interference by this administration. Two months after he was inaugurated, Trump’s Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick fired every member of PPAC and TPAC. A year and a half later, they finally swore in the first few new members.

When Congress originally authorized fee setting authority under the America Invents Act, we built in several oversight measures to ensure that this power could not be exercised without transparency but rather with public input and independent expert review. PPAC and TPAC remain a critical part of those guardrails. Their full and independent participation is essential to ensuring that fee-setting remains accountable to all who rely on our patent and trademark systems, the big and the small. That is why these committees must be fully constituted as they are a necessary safeguard for independence.

And that independence matters. If we do not give USPTO the flexibility it needs to set fees, access to our patent system will be taken over by special interests. This will make it even harder for small, independent inventors to protect their inventions and easier for those who can pay-to-play to infringe on those rights.

How do we know? Because we are already seeing this happen in the rest of the executive branch. Every day we learn again how easy it’s become for oligarchs and powerful companies to buy a seat at Donald Trump’s table. Millions of dark money in campaign contributions. Lavish gifts like private jets, and business deals. Rampant insider trading on predictive markets. Access to the Trump White House has transformed into a currency that only the rich and famous can afford.

And while the wealthy are busy buying a seat at the table, Americans across the country are left paying the price. Constituents of Georgia’s 4th Congressional district are struggling to afford rent or pay their mortgage, and the cost of groceries continue to skyrocket. Hardworking families should not struggle to afford healthcare while Elon Musk becomes a trillionaire, and while Donald Trump lines his own pockets through unabashed greed built on the backs of American taxpayers.

Conflicts of interest and self-dealing have become routine features in Trump’s Washington, blurring the line between public service and private financial gain. This was a man who campaigned on draining the swamp, and yet all Trump has done is put it behind a velvet rope and began charging an admissions fee. Because in Trump’s America money buys access. Access buys influence. And influence too often becomes the law for everyone else. Innovation should not be a luxury that only the wealthy can afford. So, I, for one, am determined to not allow USPTO to be sucked in to that swamp.

Reauthorizing this fee setting authority with the transparency, public participation, and independent oversight that Congress intended is essential to keeping our patent system working for all—not just for those with the closest connection to big tech, the aspiring oligarch class, or the Trump White House. We have just a few months to get this done. This is not time for Members or big money special interests to advocate for changes to the way the USPTO operates because they’re not happy with Director Squires’ Patent Trial and Appeals Board actions. I think we are overdue to examine proposals like Rep. Ross’s PREVAIL, which would reform PTAB abuses. I’m sure some of my colleagues on both sides of the aisle agree with me, just as others disagree. But I’m not trying to make those changes right now. We have a program that everyone agrees has been successful; inserting our own USTPO agendas into the debate will only serve to make this reauthorization controversial.

I want to thank the witnesses for being here today. While I think this hearing is unnecessary and a distraction from the disastrous policies of the Trump Administration, I do believe it is vital that Americans truly understand the importance of allowing this agency the independence and discretion it needs to keep America at the top of our global innovation economy. Because if we want to continue to lead the world in the technological advancements of tomorrow, then we must ensure today that the institution most responsible for protecting those innovations is independent and built to last.

I yield back the balance of my time.

title: Congressman Pat Harrigan Votes to Expand American Mining and Reduce Dependence on China
text:
Contact: Lexi Kranich (814) 380-4408

WASHINGTON, D.C.—Today, Congressman Pat Harrigan (NC-10) voted for H.R. 1501, the Protecting Domestic Mining Act of 2025, legislation that strengthens domestic mineral production by making the federal permitting process more predictable for American mining and mineral processing projects.

“Everything from our cars and power grid to our factories and weapons systems depends on minerals that have to be mined and processed somewhere. When we make it nearly impossible to produce those resources here at home, we don’t stop mining, we simply push it overseas and become more dependent on countries like China,” said Congressman Harrigan. “That dependence makes our supply chains more fragile, drives investment and jobs out of the United States, and gives our adversaries leverage over resources our economy and national security depend on. We can maintain strong environmental standards without trapping American projects in years of uncertainty, and this bill gives companies a clearer path to invest, build, and produce here at home.”

The Protecting Domestic Mining Act permanently adds mining and mineral processing to the sectors eligible for FAST-41, giving qualifying projects access to a coordinated federal permitting process with greater transparency and predictability. The bill also blocks a Biden-era proposed rule that would have narrowed mining eligibility under FAST-41. Projects remain subject to federal environmental requirements, but American producers gain greater certainty that access to the permitting process will not change every time a new administration takes office.

title: Harshbarger Introduces Resolution Honoring Life and Legacy of Dolly Parton, Leads Moment of Silence on House Floor
text:
Washington, D.C. — Congresswoman Diana Harshbarger (R-TN) today introduced a resolution honoring the life and legacy of Dolly Parton, the Sevier County native whose music, generosity, and devotion to her East Tennessee roots continue to touch the lives of millions following her passing on Aug. 25, 2026, in Nashville, at age 80. The resolution was co-led by Congressman John Rose (R-TN) and cosponsored by the entire Tennessee House delegation. Harshbarger also led a moment of silence on the House Floor this evening in Parton's honor.

“Dolly Parton was one of our own, and she never forgot where she came from,” said Congresswoman Diana Harshbarger. “Her music told the truth about hard work, faith, and family, and that truth is why the whole world fell in love with her. But it was her heart that made her a legend at home. Whether she was rebuilding after the wildfires that tore through her own community, opening doors for children to learn to read, supporting healthcare and research for Tennessee families, or protecting the mountains she loved, Dolly gave back every chance she got. Guided by her faith and shaped by her East Tennessee upbringing, she used her success to lift up the people around her at every turn. My prayers are with her family and everyone who loved her, and I am honored to lead this effort in the House to make sure her legacy is remembered for generations to come.”

“We couldn’t have asked for a better ambassador for Tennessee than Dolly Parton,” said Congressman John Rose. “She will continue to touch countless lives through her music and philanthropy, including the Imagination Library, and her impact on tourism in East Tennessee will be felt for decades to come. I was honored to sign onto this resolution which recognizes her extraordinary life.”

“Dolly Parton embodied everything it meant to be an East Tennessean. Her voice, her style, and her outlook on life were all born from her upbringing in Sevierville. She rose from a poor, rural farmhouse to the peaks of stardom, never forgetting the people and the place that helped her get there. The American Dream resonates with every person in this country, and as much as we love to claim her in Tennessee, she represented all of America. Rest in peace, Dolly,” said Congressman Tim Burchett.

“Dolly was a living embodiment of grace, unwavering love and support, and generosity. She was the greatest representative of Tennessee ever. Not just from her musical talents and her philanthropy, but from her big heart and outstanding generosity. She made us all proud. The world would be a better place if more people were like Dolly,” said Congressman Steve Cohen.

“Not one Tennessean has ever done more for our great state than Dolly Parton. I am proud to co-sponsor this resolution to honor her life and legacy of always putting others first,” said Congressman Scott DesJarlais.

“As we mourn the passing of Dolly Parton, we remember not only a legendary voice but a true Tennessee treasure. Dolly’s kindness, generosity, and unwavering spirit brought pride to our state and joy to millions around the world. Her remarkable legacy in music, philanthropy, and the hearts of so many will never be forgotten. From the Smoky Mountains of East Tennessee to stages worldwide, Dolly embodied the best of our community's values and touched lives everywhere she went. We honor her memory and give thanks for the extraordinary life she shared with all of us," said Congressman Chuck Fleischmann.

“I am honored to cosponsor this resolution recognizing the life and legacy of Dolly Parton,” said Congressman David Kustoff. “Dolly brought pride to our state and joy to millions. Dolly’s legacy will remain a part of Tennessee and our nation for generations to come.”

“Tennessee has lost one of its brightest stars,” said Congressman Andy Ogles. “Dolly Parton was a model Tennessean. A woman of faith, humility, generosity, and extraordinary talent who never forgot where she came from. Our prayers are with Dolly’s family and all those mourning this tremendous loss. Tennessee will never be the same without her.”

“Dolly Parton represented the very best of Tennessee, and her loss is being felt around the world. She grew up one of twelve children in a two-room cabin in the mountains of East Tennessee, and no matter how far her career took her, she never forgot where she came from. While widely known for her music and acting, her philanthropic work left its own legacy as well. When wildfires devastated Sevier County in 2016, Dolly stepped in and provided more than 900 families who had lost their homes with $10,000 each. In addition to her many other charitable gifts, her commitment to giving back also led her to establish the Imagination Library in 1995, which began in her home county and grew into a worldwide program that has provided more than 330 million free books to children. While Dolly was always proud to call Tennessee home, Tennessee could not have been prouder to call her one of our own. We will miss her dearly," said Congressman Matt Van Epps.

“Dolly Parton was a Tennessee treasure who lived out the Volunteer Spirit, loved our nation, and opened doors of opportunity for countless people,” said Senator Marsha Blackburn. “While there are no words to fully express the sorrow all Tennesseans feel in her loss, I hope this resolution plays at least a small part in ensuring that her legacy is never forgotten, and I am honored to lead it in the Senate.”

“Dolly is truly a Tennessee legend,” said Senator Bill Hagerty. “From her humble beginnings in the foothills of the Great Smoky Mountains to worldwide fame, Dolly exemplified the American Dream. Whether she was performing on stages across the globe, creating opportunities for families to make memories in Dollywood, or fostering a love of reading through her Imagination Library, Dolly lived a life dedicated to encouraging others to dream just as boldly as she did. She never forgot where she came from and left an indelible cultural and economic impact on our state. She will be very dearly missed.”

title: Comisionado Residente anuncia $351,000 en fondos federales para apoyar pequeños negocios en comunidades rurales de Puerto Rico.
text:
Image

September 2, 2026

WASHINGTON, DC — El Comisionado Residente de Puerto Rico, Pablo José Hernández Rivera, anunció $351,000 en fondos federales del programa Rural Business Development Grants de USDA Rural Development para seis proyectos dirigidos a apoyar pequeños y nuevos negocios en comunidades rurales de Puerto Rico.

Los proyectos ofrecerán capacitación, asistencia técnica, mentoría, planificación empresarial, preparación financiera y acceso a recursos para empresarios y pequeñas empresas en distintos municipios de la isla.

“Mi prioridad es impulsar el desarrollo económico y asegurar que Puerto Rico pueda aprovechar los programas y fondos federales disponibles. Estos fondos ayudarán a pequeños negocios en comunidades rurales a crecer, crear empleos y tener acceso a las herramientas que necesitan para seguir adelante”, dijo el Comisionado Residente.

Las subvenciones aprobadas son:

Asesores Financieros Comunitarios, Inc. — $64,200: ofrecerá un programa de 12 meses para 25 negocios rurales en Aibonito, Barranquitas, Cidra y Naranjito, con diagnósticos empresariales, planes de trabajo individualizados, asistencia técnica semanal y diez talleres. El proyecto busca apoyar 20 empleos existentes y crear cinco nuevos.

Causa Local Corporation — $30,000: ofrecerá asistencia técnica a aproximadamente 25 negocios rurales, incluyendo educación empresarial, capacitación en manejo financiero, planificación de negocios, preparación para acceso a capital y recursos empresariales. El proyecto busca crear siete empleos y preservar 17. El Comisionado Residente respaldó previamente este proyecto mediante una carta de apoyo para impulsar su consideración para fondos federales.

Centro para Emprendedores, Inc. — $64,200: implementará la iniciativa NUCLEO Rural Business Development & Technical Assistance para 15 negocios rurales, con un programa de diez semanas que incluye diagnósticos, mentoría individual, asistencia técnica y diez talleres educativos. El proyecto busca preservar 15 empleos.

Fondo de Inversión y Desarrollo Cooperativo (FIDECOOP) — $64,200: desarrollará Generation Coop, con capacitación, asistencia técnica y asesoría empresarial para más de 40 participantes en municipios y comunidades rurales de Puerto Rico. El proyecto busca crear 30 empleos.

Friends of Puerto Rico — $64,200: implementará el Rural Innovation & Business Growth Accelerator para 75 negocios rurales en San Sebastián, Isabela y Aguadilla, con énfasis en competitividad, productividad, adopción de tecnología y crecimiento. El proyecto busca crear 30 empleos y preservar 30.

Operation HOPE, Inc. — $64,200: ofrecerá asistencia técnica a 25 pequeños y nuevos negocios en Aguas Buenas, Lares, Las Piedras, Manatí, Ponce y Utuado mediante talleres, mentoría individual y herramientas de comercio electrónico. El proyecto busca crear 12 empleos.

En conjunto, las seis subvenciones representan $351,000 en fondos federales. Los proyectos contemplan atender 165 negocios rurales, además de más de 40 participantes en el proyecto de FIDECOOP, y busca la creación de 84 empleos y la preservación de 112 empleos.

El Comisionado Residente continuará trabajando para ampliar el acceso de Puerto Rico a programas y fondos federales que apoyen a los pequeños negocios, fortalezcan las comunidades rurales y fomenten nuevas oportunidades económicas.

title: COMISIONADO RESIDENTE DETALLA ESCÁNDALO DE POWER EXPECTATIONS EN HEMICICLO CAMERAL — EXIGE RENDICIÓN DE CUENTAS
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — El Comisionado Residente de Puerto Rico, Pablo José Hernández Rivera, detalló en el hemiciclo de la Cámara de Representantes la cronología del controversial contrato de $5,900 millones para generación de energía temporera en Puerto Rico. En su mensaje, exigió rendición de cuentas a las agencias gubernamentales responsables de supervisarlo y anunció que haría solicitudes de información conforme a su autoridad congresional.

El Comisionado Residente señaló que él y el excongresista Mark Greene plantearon preocupaciones bipartitas sobre irregularidades en el proceso de contratación el año pasado.

"Parece que la preocupación estaba justificada", dijo el Comisionado Residente.

El Comisionado Residente narró que el 28 de agosto de 2025, Power Expectations y Reyes Contractor obtuvieron un contrato de $5,900 millones para generación de energía temporera en Puerto Rico, pese a carecer de la pericia y capacidad financiera requeridas. El gobierno les ordenó formar un consorcio, y así incorporaron a Enchanted Rock, cuyo contrato fue firmado por una persona identificada como "Jhoby Weaks" —un puesto y una firma que, días después, Enchanted Rock denunció como falsos. Según el Comisionado Residente, la empresa también había recibido previamente una carta de un bufete que intentó extorsionarla, carta que el propio bufete luego negó haber enviado.

En lugar de rescindir el contrato o denunciar el fraude, las agencias responsables sustituyeron discretamente a Enchanted Rock por otra empresa. Casi dos meses después, trascendió el alegado fraude. Tras conocerse la noticia, la Junta canceló el contrato, y el gobierno, bajo presión pública, refirió el caso a las autoridades casi dos meses después de haberse enterado.

El Comisionado Residente exhortó al gobierno de Puerto Rico a rendir cuentas, señalando que el Congreso ha asignado $17,000 millones para proyectos de energía en la isla. Insistió en que buscará respuestas sobre qué sabía el gobierno, cuándo lo supo, por qué lo ocultó, y si el episodio refleja corrupción, incompetencia o ambas. También señaló las consecuencias reales del escándalo: apagones causados por la consiguiente falta de capacidad de generación de emergencia.

"El pueblo de Puerto Rico merece respuestas y rendición de cuentas. El Congreso, que ha asignado $17,000 millones para proyectos de energía en Puerto Rico, merece respuestas y rendición de cuentas", dijo el Comisionado Residente. "La gran mayoría de los puertorriqueños no somos corruptos ni incompetentes. Como la gran mayoría de los ciudadanos americanos y de los miembros del Congreso, detestamos la corrupción y le hacemos frente. Trabajemos juntos para restaurar el buen gobierno, castigar la corrupción, arreglar lo básico y volver a encender las luces en Puerto Rico."

HERNÁNDEZ: FORGED SIGNATURE, HIDDEN FRAUD TAINT $5.9 BILLION PUERTO RICO ENERGY CONTRACT — DEMANDS ACCOUNTABILITY

WATCH the full video HERE.

Resident Commissioner says the government of Puerto Rico knew about the forgery and covered it up for nearly two months while Puerto Ricans suffered power outages

WASHINGTON, DC — Puerto Rico Resident Commissioner Pablo José Hernández took to the floor of the U.S. House of Representatives to detail what he called a forged signature and cover-up at the heart of a $5.9 billion contract for temporary energy generation in Puerto Rico, and to demand accountability from the government agencies responsible for overseeing it.

Hernández noted that he and former Congressman Mark Greene raised bipartisan concerns about irregularities in the procurement process last year, cosigning a letter to the relevant agencies that went unanswered.

"It appears the concern was warranted," Hernández said.

According to Hernández, on August 28, 2025, Power Expectations and Reyes Contractor were awarded a $5.9 billion contract for temporary energy generation in Puerto Rico. Because the companies lacked the required expertise and financial capacity to perform the contract, the government agency overseeing the procurement directed them to find a partner and form a consortium.

Power Expectations and Reyes Contractor subsequently brought in Enchanted Rock, with a person identified as "Jhoby Weaks," described as "COO-Caribbean Operations," signing the contract on Enchanted Rock's behalf. The Financial Oversight and Management Board, which must approve contracts over $10 million, authorized the deal.

Days later, Hernández said, Enchanted Rock informed the government of Puerto Rico that it had not signed the contract — that "Jhoby Weaks" was not an Enchanted Rock employee, that the company had no "COO-Caribbean Operations" position, and that its signature had been forged.

Hernández further stated that before the alleged forged signature, Enchanted Rock received a letter from a law firm that the company said attempted to blackmail it. When Enchanted Rock followed up, the law firm denied sending the letter and denied ever representing Power Expectations or Reyes Contractor — indicating, according to Hernández, that the letter itself was also forged.

Rather than rescind the contract or report the apparent fraud, Hernández said the responsible government agencies quietly substituted Enchanted Rock with another company through an Assignment and Assumption Agreement.

Nearly two months later, an investigative journalist revealed that a signature had been forged on the $5.9 billion contract. Hernández said the government of Puerto Rico had known about the forgery and withheld that information from the public, the Puerto Rico Electric Power Authority, and the Oversight Board. Following the report, the Oversight Board canceled the contract, and the government, under public pressure, referred the matter to law enforcement nearly two months after first learning of the forgery.

Hernández called on the government of Puerto Rico to provide answers, noting that Congress has appropriated $17 billion for energy projects on the island. He pressed for answers to what the government knew, when it knew it, why it was concealed, and whether the episode reflects corruption, incompetence, or both. He also pointed to the real-world consequences of the scandal: power outages caused by the resulting lack of emergency generation capacity.

"The people of Puerto Rico deserve answers and accountability. Congress, which has assigned $17 billion for energy projects in Puerto Rico, deserves answers and accountability," Hernández said. "The vast majority of Puerto Ricans are neither corrupt nor incompetent. Like the vast majority of our fellow American citizens and members of Congress, we detest corruption and we stand up to it. Let's work together to restore good governance, punish corruption, fix the basics, and turn the lights back on in Puerto Rico.”

title: House Republicans Pass Bills to Push North Atlantic Right Whales Toward Extinction, Let Trump Fast-Track Permits for Any Mine He Likes
text:
Washington, D.C. — House Natural Resources Committee Ranking Member Jared Huffman (D-Calif.) took to the House Floor this week to oppose H.R. 9436, which extends a special industry waiver that will lead to more critically endangered North Atlantic right whales dying in fishing rope, and H.R. 1501, which lets the Trump administration fast-track any mining project, including those the Trump family has invested in.

“This bill sells our fishing communities a false promise. We may hear that kicking the can down the road saves the Maine lobster fleet. In reality, this bill would lock in a broken status quo that guarantees disaster for both our historic coastal industry and the critically endangered right whale,” said Ranking Member Huffman on H.R. 9436.

“NOAA is lying down on the job, dragging its feet, firing staff, axing science and deprioritizing ropeless gear, perhaps because they think Congress will bail them out and kick the can a little further down the road. All of this is illegal, and all of it is causing massive uncertainty for the lobster fishery. Now, two years ahead of the deadline, this bill would add another seven-year delay instead of holding NOAA accountable. The solution already exists. Ropeless gear reduces deadly entanglements of whales without sacrificing catch. Fishermen are actively testing and using ropeless gear right now. They’ve landed over one million pounds of seafood using these methods. Let’s stop pretending that House Republicans and this administration care about fishermen, coastal communities, or these iconic whales. If Congress can arbitrarily grant a decade-plus statutory exemption to bypass protections for a critically endangered species, the Endangered Species Act is reduced to a hollow suggestion.”

On H.R. 1501, Ranking Member Huffman said, “It is our third day back from a five-week recess. We have 15 days left here in Washington before the election. It should be a time that we're trying to get some real work done. But instead of doing that, instead of doing a single thing to help our constituents who are struggling under skyrocketing costs of groceries, gas and electricity bills, Republicans are scraping the bottom of the barrel to come up with any bill that their chaotic conference can find a way to pass. And one of the surest ways, it seems, is to find a way to do another favor for the president's friends and for foreign owned mining conglomerates. But here's the thing, Mr. Speaker. We've just heard the main rationale for this bill that we've got to make sure critical minerals mining projects and the processing projects for those critical minerals are eligible for FAST-41. They've made it sound as if today's bill would finally make that possible.”

“Well, I have a news flash for everyone. Mining is already a covered sector. Under a regulation adopted during the first Trump administration. Mineral processing projects are also allowed on FAST-41 as manufacturing. So we have an advertised solution here to a problem that does not exist. So what is this bill all about? Well, that's the other half of the bill. The part that would potentially tie the hands of this and future administrations from using FAST-41 in a smart and targeted way that would focus on actual critical minerals projects that were in our national interest, that were all about our national competitiveness. How does that make America more secure? The answer is it doesn't.”

Background

H.R. 9436, sponsored by Rep. Mike Lawler (R-N.Y.), extends a six-year Endangered Species Act and Marine Mammal Protection Act waiver for the American lobster and Jonah crab fisheries of Maine, Massachusetts, and Rhode Island from 2028 to 2035. Kicking the can down the road another seven years disincentivizes progress on gear that supports a robust fishery and keeps whales safe. Congress has already appropriated approximately $280 million for right whale recovery, including $20 million for innovative fishing technologies, and there are two more years to assess the latest data before setting new policy.

Only about 380 North Atlantic right whales remain, including 70 females of reproductive age, and the species can sustain less than one human-caused death per year. More than 85 percent have become entangled in fishing gear at least once, and so far in 2026 two right whales have died due to a gear entanglement and a vessel strike.

H.R. 1501, sponsored by Rep. Jefferson Shreve (R-Ind.), codifies mining and mineral processing as covered sectors under FAST-41, a permitting pathway with restrictions on public input and judicial review. Mining and mineral processing are already eligible for FAST-41 under current regulations, so the bill changes nothing for the mining sector but leaves the door open for political favoritism in permitting. Committee Republicans voted down a Democratic amendment to focus on critical minerals, allowing the Trump administration to give special treatment to any mine they like, including projects the Trump family has invested in.

FAST-41 judicial review provisions can make it harder to stop mining projects that threaten wildlife and nearby populations, and its timelines can undermine Tribal consultation and Tribal sovereignty, compounding problems created by the antiquated Mining Law of 1872.

title: REP. IVEY LEADS BIPARTISAN CODEL TO WITNESS SUCCESSFUL LAUNCH OF NANCY GRACE ROMAN SPACE TELESCOPE
text:
Image

WASHINGTON — Congressman Glenn Ivey (MD-04) led a bipartisan delegation of Members of Congress to Cape Canaveral, Florida, from Saturday, August 29 through Monday, August 31, in partnership with the U.S. Space Force and NASA, to witness the successful launch of NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope.

The Roman Space Telescope lifted off aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket at 7:26 a.m. EDT on Sunday, August 30, from Launch Complex 39A at NASA's Kennedy Space Center, and reached orbit roughly 10 minutes later. The delegation observed the launch in person and met with Space Force and NASA leadership to discuss the future of the U.S. space and space science enterprise.

“The successful launch of the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is a tremendous achievement for NASA and a proud moment for Maryland. I congratulate the exceptional NASA Goddard workforce and every partner whose expertise and dedication made this mission possible—especially nine months ahead of schedule and under budget. This observatory will reveal to us distant worlds, helping us understand dark matter and dark energy, and inspire the imagination of the next generation. Goddard’s critical scientific missions continue to reaffirm America’s global leadership in space science and will now advance discovery for years to come,” said Congressman Ivey, representative of Maryland’s Fourth District.

The delegation included Representatives George Whitesides (D-CA), Suhas Subramanyam (D-VA), and Mike Haridopolos (R-FL). Science communicator Bill Nye the Science Guy also joined the delegation for part of the trip.

ABOUT THE MISSION

Named for NASA's first chief astronomer, known as the “mother of Hubble,” the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is NASA's next flagship observatory and its most significant astrophysics mission since the James Webb Space Telescope. Roman carries a primary mirror with a field of view at least 100 times larger than Hubble's, enabling it to survey wide swaths of the sky to study dark energy and dark matter, search for exoplanets, and advance infrared astrophysics. The observatory launched roughly nine months ahead of its required launch readiness date and is now on a three-month journey to join Webb at the second Sun-Earth Lagrange point (L2), where it will operate collaboratively with Hubble and Webb to give humanity an unprecedented view of the universe, paving the way for future observatories in the search for signs of life beyond our solar system.

PARTNERS

Roman is a worldwide collaborative effort, featuring a network of 85 national partners across 17 states and 13 international partners across 9 countries. More information about the global network of partners contributing to this mission can be found at: https://science.nasa.gov/mission/roman-space-telescope/partners/

title: Congressman Kean Hosts Veterans Affairs Roundtable with Secretary Collins
text:
(September 2, 2026) SOMERVILLE, NJ – Last week, Congressman Tom Kean, Jr. (NJ-07) hosted a Veteran Services and Advocacy Roundtable with U.S. Secretary of Veterans Affairs Doug Collins.

The roundtable brought together federal, state, and local leaders, Veterans Service Organizations, veteran-serving nonprofits, and other veterans from New Jersey’s 7th Congressional District. Participants discussed the priorities and challenges facing veterans and their families, while working to identify solutions and strengthen the support available to those who have served.

“It is my priority to ensure that New Jersey’s veterans receive the care, benefits, and support they have earned,” said Congressman Kean. “I appreciate Secretary Collins coming to New Jersey and hearing directly from the veterans and organizations serving our communities. From the Lyons VA to local veterans’ organizations across our district, I am focused on identifying what is working, fixing what is not, and strengthening the services veterans rely on. I will continue working to cut through obstacles and make sure the men and women who served our country can access the care and support they deserve.”

“Under President Trump and thanks to the steadfast support of strong leaders like Rep. Kean, VA is making major improvements for Veterans in New Jersey and across the nation,” said VA Secretary Doug Collins. “We look forward to continuing to work with Rep. Kean to make VA benefits better, faster and easier to use than ever before.”

“The Veterans of Foreign Wars thanks Congressman Kean and Secretary Collins for their leadership and cooperation with veteran advocates to improve the lives and welfare of New Jersey's veterans,” said Ken Hagemann, VFW State Commander, Department of New Jersey.

“It was a true privilege to sit at this table. I was honored to contribute to this vital conversation with our leadership, focusing on how we can better support our veterans, their needs and valuable community presence,” said Jacquie Petersen, Warren County VSO. “Participants were given time to discuss our concerns.
